name: Crypto cash-and-carry basis trade (dated futures)

origin.source_title: Crypto carry (BIS Working Paper 1087; forthcoming Management Science)

how_it_works.simple: A bitcoin promised for next quarter often costs more than a bitcoin today. You buy one today, sell the promise, and keep the price gap when the date arrives.
how_it_works.analogy: Like buying concert tickets at face value and selling them in advance to a fan who will pay extra to lock in a seat.
how_it_works.precise: Long spot (or a spot ETF) and short a dated future of the same maturity; hold to expiry so the basis converges. The annualized basis is (F/S - 1) x 365/days to expiry. Profit is the locked-in basis minus funding cost of the spot leg, fees and margin costs.

rule: At each quarterly roll, compute the annualized basis on the next CME or exchange-listed quarterly future; if it exceeds the cash rate plus a cost hurdle (for example 3 percentage points), buy spot and short the future in equal notional and hold to expiry, otherwise hold cash.
data_needed: Quarterly futures prices (CME, Deribit, Binance, OKX)
economic_rationale: BIS working paper 1087 finds crypto carry averages above 10 percent a year and reaches up to 60 percent, driven by a volatile convenience yield from trend-chasing small investors and scarce arbitrage capital.
why_it_might_fail: The same paper finds high carry predicts crashes. After US spot ETFs launched, CoinDesk (10 Aug 2026) reported the three-month CME basis near 3 percent, below the roughly 3.8 percent two-year Treasury yield, and hedge funds flipping net long, meaning the trade no longer paid for its capital.

reported_results.source: Schmeling, Schrimpf, Todorov, BIS WP 1087 abstract page
reported_results.period: not stated on the abstract page
reported_results.market: BTC and ETH futures across crypto and traditional exchanges
reported_results.notes: The page says average carry exceeds 10 percent per year and can reach 60 percent per year. These are basis levels, not strategy returns. The full PDF could not be fetched (bot block), so no strategy Sharpe is recorded here.

reported_results.source: CoinDesk, A rare CME shift: hedge funds abandon structural shorts
reported_results.notes: Annual_return here is the quoted annualized gross basis (about 3 percent), not a realized track record. It compares with about 3.8 percent on two-year Treasuries.

post_publication_evidence: After spot ETF approval the basis trade became a crowded institutional trade; by August 2026 the CME three-month basis was about 3 percent, below Treasury yields, and hedge funds on CME turned net long (CoinDesk, 10 Aug 2026).

implementations.notes: Spot-perpetual and cross-exchange arbitrage connectors can be adapted; dated futures need user code.

relevance.reason: Mirrors covered interest parity and FX forward points, but returns now sit near the cash rate so it is unlikely to beat the S&P 500.
